mediaChecklist.label: Every camera card and audio source has been copied and opened.
A second verified backup exists on a separate device.
Original media remains unchanged and separate from working files.
Picture, production sound, and sync relationships have been checked.
Missing, damaged, silent, or incomplete material is recorded in a problem log.
Recording media will not be erased until backups and working files are verified.

principles.title: Edit from evidence
principles.text: Let recorded behavior, words, actions, environments, and sound determine what the film can honestly claim.

principles.title: Meaning lives between shots
principles.text: A shot changes when it follows another. Review the relationship you create, not only the quality of each isolated image.

principles.title: Complete the dramatic event
principles.text: A scene needs enough action, reaction, detail, voice, and sound for the audience to experience what changes.

principles.title: Preserve context
principles.text: Do not manufacture chronology, causality, consent, or emotion that the recorded situation cannot support.

clipFunctions.label: Create a turn, obstacle, or decision

example.title: After the Tide
example.disclosure: Fictional coastal-cleanup teaching material; not documentary evidence.
example.question: Can organizer Mara keep volunteers safe, adapt to worsening weather, and leave the shoreline meaningfully changed?

clips.label: Empty shoreline before dawn
clips.description: Wind moves discarded plastic along the tide line before anyone arrives.

clips.label: Mara arrives and unlocks the equipment trailer
clips.description: Mara checks the sky, opens the trailer, and begins unloading gloves and collection bags.

clips.label: Volunteer safety briefing
clips.description: Mara identifies sharp waste, the incoming storm, and the agreed stopping conditions.

clips.label: Cleanup and sorting sequence
clips.description: Hands collect, weigh, separate, and bag material while volunteers communicate across the beach.

clips.label: Weather interrupts the plan
clips.description: Rain begins, one collection station collapses, and a volunteer asks whether the group should stop.
clips.sound: Rain, flapping tarp, question off camera

clips.label: Mara changes the operation
clips.description: Mara closes the exposed station and moves the group to the sheltered end of the beach.

clips.label: Final weigh-in under shelter
clips.description: The team weighs the recovered material and compares it with the morning estimate.
clips.sound: Scale click, group reaction, quiet conversation

clips.label: Mara reflects after the volunteers leave
clips.description: Mara considers what the team achieved and what the tide may return overnight.

clips.label: Shoreline after the cleanup
clips.description: The beach is quieter and visibly changed, but small fragments remain near the water.

roughCutScenes.title: Before the volunteers arrive
roughCutScenes.summary: The shore, Mara, and the day's practical and ethical question are established.

roughCutScenes.title: The cleanup becomes collective action
roughCutScenes.summary: The briefing becomes behavior as the volunteers collect and sort material.

roughCutScenes.title: Weather tests the plan
roughCutScenes.summary: Conditions force a safety decision and reveal Mara's leadership.

roughCutScenes.title: Evidence and consequence
roughCutScenes.summary: The final weigh-in, reflection, and changed shoreline answer the opening question without claiming permanence.
